prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1495; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a sideswipe while changing lanes and described contact along the passenger side of the vehicle. The claimant mentioned a knee injury from the impact and said they were not represented by a lawyer.

Entry 2: Photos taken at the scene confirm some of the details the claimant gave, although no independent witnesses have come forward. The police report and the people who stopped to help both confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 3: The damage to the vehicle is mostly in line with the impact described, and the pattern of the scrapes and dents fits a sideswipe. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage. The driver is named on the policy.

Entry 4: The reported knee injury matches the kind and force of a crash like this one. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from the claimant's history or prior claims.

Entry 5: The claimant has given the same account of the accident in every conversation so far, including the sequence of the lane change and the point of contact. Treatment has followed a usual course, with visits tapering off as the claimant's knee improved.

Entry 6: Based on the photos, the statement, the police confirmation, and the medical timeline, the file is consistent and no open questions remain on liability or the reported injury. The claim is ready for the next review step.
